{{short description|Theorem on constructible abelian sheaves over the spectrum of a ring of algebraic numbers}}
In [[mathematics]], '''Artin–Verdier duality''' is a [[duality (mathematics)|duality]] theorem for constructible abelian [[sheaf (mathematics)|sheaves]] over the [[spectrum of a ring]] of [[algebraic number]]s, introduced by {{harvs|txt|last1=Artin|first1=Michael|authorlink1=Michael Artin| last2= Verdier |first2=Jean-Louis|authorlink2=Jean-Louis Verdier|year=1964}}, that generalizes [[Tate duality]].

It shows that, as far as [[Étale cohomology|etale]] (or [[Flat cohomology|flat]]) [[cohomology]] is concerned, the [[ring of integers]] in a [[Algebraic number field|number field]] behaves like a [[3-manifold|3-dimensional]] [[mathematical object]].

== Statement ==
Let ''X'' be the [[spectrum of a ring|spectrum]] of the [[ring of integers]] in a [[totally imaginary number field|totally imaginary]] [[number field]] ''K'', and ''F'' a [[constructible sheaf|constructible]] [[étale topology|étale]] [[abelian sheaf]] on ''X''. Then the [[Yoneda product|Yoneda pairing]]

:<math>H^r(X,F)\times \operatorname{Ext}^{3-r}(F,\mathbb{G}_m)\to H^3(X,\mathbb{G}_m)=\Q/\Z </math>

is a [[pairing|non-degenerate pairing]] of finite abelian groups, for every integer ''r''.

Here, ''H<sup>r</sup>''(''X,F'') is the ''r''-th [[étale cohomology]] group of the [[scheme (mathematics)|scheme]] ''X'' with values in ''F,'' and Ext''<sup>r</sup>''(''F,G'') is the group of ''r''-[[ext functor|extensions]] of the étale sheaf ''G'' by the étale sheaf ''F'' in the [[abelian category|category]] of étale abelian sheaves on ''X.'' Moreover, ''G<sub>m</sub>'' denotes the étale sheaf of [[unit (ring theory)|units]] in the [[structure sheaf]] of ''X.''

{{harvs|txt|last=Deninger|first=Christopher|authorlink=Christopher Deninger|year=1986}} proved Artin–Verdier duality for constructible, but not necessarily torsion sheaves. For such a sheaf ''F'', the above pairing induces isomorphisms

:<math>\begin{align}
H^r(X, F)^* &\cong \operatorname{Ext}^{3-r}(F, \mathbb{G}_m) && r = 0, 1 \\
H^r(X, F) &\cong \operatorname{Ext}^{3-r}(F, \mathbb{G}_m)^* && r = 2, 3 
\end{align}</math>

where 

:<math>(-)^* = \operatorname{Hom}(-, \Q /\Z).</math>

== Finite flat group schemes ==
Let ''U'' be an open subscheme of the spectrum of the ring of integers in a number field ''K'', and ''F'' a finite flat commutative [[group scheme]] over ''U''. Then the [[cup product]] defines a non-degenerate pairing

:<math>H^r(U,F^D)\times H_c^{3-r}(U,F)\to H_c^3(U,{\mathbb G}_m)=\Q/\Z</math>

of finite abelian groups, for all integers ''r''.

Here ''F<sup>D</sup>'' denotes the [[Cartier dual]] of ''F'', which is another finite flat commutative group scheme over ''U''. Moreover, <math>H^r(U,F)</math> is the ''r''-th [[Flat topology|flat cohomology]] group of the scheme ''U'' with values in the flat abelian sheaf ''F'', and <math>H_c^r(U,F)</math> is the ''r''-th ''flat cohomology with compact supports'' of ''U'' with values in the flat abelian sheaf ''F.''

The ''flat cohomology with compact supports'' is defined to give rise to a long exact sequence

:<math>\cdots\to H^r_c(U,F)\to H^r(U,F)\to \bigoplus\nolimits_{v\notin U} H^r(K_v,F)\to H^{r+1}_c(U,F) \to\cdots</math>

The sum is taken over all [[Place (mathematics)|places]] of ''K'', which are not in ''U'', including the archimedean ones. The local contribution ''H<sup>r</sup>''(''K<sub>v</sub>'', ''F'') is the [[Galois cohomology]] of the [[Henselization]] ''K<sub>v</sub>'' of ''K'' at the place ''v'', modified a la [[Tate cohomology group|Tate]]:

:<math>H^r(K_v,F)=H^r_T(\mathrm{Gal}(K_v^s/K_v),F(K_v^s)).</math>

Here <math>K_v^s</math> is a separable closure of <math>K_v.</math>
